keyVerseText: Then Esther the queen, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew, wrote with all authority, to confirm this second letter of Purim. authority: Heb. strength
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun תֹּקֶף (tôqeph) derives from the root תָּקַף (tâqaph), which means to prevail, overpower, or overcome. This root sense conveys not just physical strength but an active exertion of power to dominate or have authority over something. Thus, the noun form carries the idea of inherent strength or power that enables prevailing, going beyond a mere abstract concept of strength to imply effective and authoritative force.
usageInScripture: The word תֹּקֶף appears three times in Scripture and is consistently associated with concepts of authority, power, and strength. It is translated variously as 'with all authority,' 'of his power,' and 'with the strength,' reflecting a spectrum that includes both literal physical strength and figurative authoritative power. This range shows the word’s flexibility in describing both tangible and intangible forms of strength, always emphasizing the capacity to exert influence or control.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding תֹּקֶף as rooted in prevailing power enriches our grasp of divine authority in Scripture. It reminds believers that God’s power is not passive but active and prevailing, able to overcome opposition and establish His will. This word highlights the reality of God’s sovereign strength working in history and in the lives of His people. For the Christian faith, it underscores the confidence we can have in God's overpowering grace and authority through Christ, who prevails over sin and death.
keyVerseReflection: In Esther 9:29, the phrase 'wrote with all authority' (Hebrew strength) emphasizes the decisive and authoritative nature of the letter confirming Purim. The use of תֹּקֶף here underscores that the decree was not merely a suggestion but carried the full weight and power of royal command. This reflects how God’s providential strength can work through human authority to accomplish His purposes.
